about: Benchmark entry G01 (train split) in dev.json format. Tier 4: a small electronics enclosure with a catalogue board placed by datums, a plug-envelope opening, three catalogue LEDs in lid holes, a snap-fit lid and standoffs, judged by interference, clearance and snap-fit checks on the delivered STLs. L1 ids match benchmarks/generalize/designs/G01/requirements.md. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and the part.json catalogue.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (stability, connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the board in, load path)

requests.title: Arduino Nano box with snap lid
requests.request: I need a small box for an Arduino Nano (board 45 x 18 mm) that I will leave on a shelf. The Nano's mini-USB port has to be reachable through one short end of the box with the lid on, so I can plug a cable in. Three 5 mm status LEDs, separate parts wired to the Nano, sit in the top face of the lid and must be visible from outside. The lid snaps on without screws, so the box has no fasteners at all. The Nano keeps its header pins pointing down (they stick out of the underside), so the board has to stand clear of the floor. The base is printed flat on the bed in PLA, with no supports.
requests.request_verbatim: I need a small box for an Arduino Nano that I will leave on a shelf. The mini-USB port has to be reachable through one short end with the lid on, and three 5 mm status LEDs on the top face should be visible. The lid snaps on without screws and the base is printed flat in PLA.
requests.request_notes: Added to the brief (derived, see requirements.md 3.1 and 3.2): 'top face' = the lid's top (FD2); the LEDs are separate 5 mm LEDs in lid holes (FD3); the Nano is held on four posts under its holes with locating pins (FD1); the header tails point down as supplied (A2); lid snap = cantilever hooks on the long sides (FD4); PLA FDM (A7).

l1.text: The design shall place the Arduino Nano from the catalogue with its mini-USB port facing one short (18 mm) end and three 5 mm LEDs on the lid, without the parts colliding, and shall declare that layout.
The 45 x 18 x 1.6 mm board shall fit inside the closed box with at least 0.5 mm clearance to every printed surface, except where it rests on its posts, and its USB receptacle shall be inside the box.

The board shall rest on exactly four posts, one under each mounting hole, each 3.0 to 4.0 mm across (the hole's own keep-out is 4.0) with a locating pin 0.1 to 0.3 mm smaller than the 1.7 mm hole going through it, with its header tails clear of the floor.
With the lid closed, nothing shall come within 5.0 mm above the board's top surface, nor within 0.3 mm of the header bodies and pin tails below it.

With the lid closed, a mini-USB cable shall plug fully into the Nano through one opening in the −X end wall with at least 0.3 mm to spare all round the plug, leaving at least 1.5 mm of wall between the opening and the lid seam, the floor and the corners, and the opening shall be no more than 1.5 mm bigger than the plug on any side.

The lid shall hold three 5 mm LEDs with their lenses through 5.2 to 5.4 mm holes in its top face and their flanges captured behind it, so each dome is visible from outside and the LED cannot be pulled out of the front (flange overlap on the hole at least 0.2 mm per side). The three LEDs sit in a row over the board, at least 9.0 mm apart and at least 4.0 mm from the cavity edge.

The lid shall be held by snap hooks only, with no screw or other fastener, with at least two hooks on each long side and none at the end walls, each hook at least 5 mm wide and engaging 0.6 to 1.0 mm, on an arm whose bending strain 1.5 t y / L^2 (thickness t, engagement y, free length L) stays at or below 0.02.
The lid shall be a separate body that locates on the base with a sliding lip (at least 2.0 mm deep, 0.15 to 0.35 mm per side clearance) and closes flush, without interpenetrating it.

The closed box shall have no openings other than the USB opening and the three LED holes, and its walls, floor and lid shall be 2.0 to 3.0 mm thick, with at least 1.5 mm of material round each opening.
The base shall print flat on its floor and the lid on its outer face, each as one manifold body without supports.
The closed box, not counting the LED domes, shall be no larger than 60 x 30 x 26 mm, longest along the board's 45 mm side, and shall stand flat on a shelf without tipping.
The design shall be delivered as a base STL, a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own clearance report, and the report shall agree with an independent measurement.

beyond_library: datum placement: the Nano's pose, its USB_MOUTH / USB_AXIS and HOLE datums set the openings and the posts
a plug-envelope opening sized from the mini-USB plug (overmold 11 x 8) and its sweep
three LED holes in a flat lid, derived from the LED's lens and flange, with a retention shoulder
a snap-fit lid: cantilever hooks with a computed strain limit, lead-in and catch faces, grooves in the base
posts and locating pins at the board's mounting holes, with a floor gap that clears the header tails
two printable bodies with their own print orientation
